definition: In computer science and operations research, Genetic fuzzy systems are fuzzy systems constructed by using genetic algorithms or genetic programming, which mimic the process of natural evolution, to identify its structure and parameter.
details: When it comes to automatically identifying and building a fuzzy system, given the high degree of nonlinearity of the output, traditional linear optimization tools have several limitations. Therefore, in the framework of soft computing, genetic algorithms (GAs) and genetic programming (GP) methods have been used successfully to identify structure and parameters of fuzzy systems.

explainer.lead: A genetic fuzzy system is a fuzzy system whose structure and parameters are discovered through evolutionary search rather than chosen entirely by hand. It is useful when highly nonlinear behavior makes traditional linear optimization tools a poor fit.

tiers.eli5: Imagine selectively breeding many versions of a set of “if…then…” rules, keeping the useful ones and changing them over several rounds. A genetic fuzzy system uses this evolutionary idea to find both the rules’ organization and their settings.
tiers.practitioner: Practitioners apply genetic algorithms or genetic programming to identify a fuzzy system’s structure and parameter values. This soft-computing approach is motivated by highly nonlinear outputs; treating the construction problem as conventional linear optimization can run into limitations.
tiers.paperLevel: Given a fuzzy system F(s, p), search over its structure s and parameters p using a genetic algorithm or genetic programming, with evolution-inspired operations guiding system identification. The approach addresses the limitations of traditional linear optimization when the output is highly nonlinear.

explainer.example: Suppose an engineer wants a fuzzy controller with rules such as “if temperature is high, increase cooling,” but does not know the best rule structure or numeric settings. A genetic algorithm evolves candidate controllers, producing a fuzzy system whose structure and parameters were found through that search.

usedIn.name: Computer science
usedIn.detail: Constructing fuzzy systems with genetic algorithms or genetic programming.

usedIn.name: Operations research
usedIn.detail: Identifying fuzzy-system structure and parameters when outputs are highly nonlinear.

usedIn.name: Soft computing
usedIn.detail: Using GA and GP methods for automatic fuzzy-system identification.

explainer.intuition: Instead of designing every part of a fuzzy system manually, create and evolve candidate designs. Natural evolution supplies the inspiration for searching through possible structures and parameter settings.
howItWorks: Start with a fuzzy system whose structure and parameters must be identified.
Represent candidate structures and parameter settings for evolutionary search.
Use a genetic algorithm or genetic programming to generate and change candidates.
Select candidates according to how well they perform the intended task.
Return the evolved fuzzy system with its identified structure and parameters.
explainer.whyItMatters: It automates the identification of fuzzy systems, including both their structure and parameters. It also provides an alternative when highly nonlinear outputs limit traditional linear optimization tools.
misconceptions: It is not simply a fuzzy system monitored by a genetic algorithm; evolution is used to construct the system.
It is not a linear optimization technique; nonlinearity is a key reason for using it.

diagram.caption: Evolutionary search repeatedly generates and evaluates fuzzy-system candidates until a structure and parameter set are selected.
